VistaRemote uses a hybrid model—not pure RBAC and not pure ABAC:

Authenticate (JWT) → Plan entitlements → RBAC (job role) → ABAC (resource) → allow/deny + audit

Normative spec: spec/authorization-spec.md in the Meta-Repo.

RBAC or ABAC?

Model	Standalone?	Role here
RBAC	No (one layer)	Stable job roles: platform super_admin / admin / viewer; org org_owner / it_support / member, etc.
ABAC	No (one layer)	Resource scope: ownerId, orgId, allowOrgSupport, room membership
Plan	Third layer	free / pro / enterprise for commercial features (recording, AI, enterprise security)

Two “admin” concepts

Account	App	Typical user
Platform admin	web/apps/admin	SaaS operators
Org user (client)	web/apps/client, mobile	Employees, executives, IT support

IT support uses the client app with orgRole=it_support. Platform operators use admin JWT for global user/plan management.

Persona mapping

Business label	Technical setup
Employee	User member
Executive / owner	User org_owner + Enterprise plan
IT support	User it_support + device allowOrgSupport
Platform admin	Admin admin / super_admin
Compliance read-only	Admin viewer or User security_auditor

Channel	Credential
Client REST	Controller JWT
Admin REST	Admin JWT
WSS /signaling	Short-lived Signaling ticket
SSE /api/v1/events/stream	Controller or Admin JWT; userId must match sub

Policy helpers live in shared/src/auth/; WSS/SSE handshake enforcement is P3 (FR-MSG-10/11).

server/src/auth/     # PolicyService (Nest)

title: Cross-platform stack: why not Flutter
content:
Product narrative for executives, operations, and developers: Technical advantages.

VistaRemote uses React + TypeScript for Web, Electron desktop, and React Native mobile UI. We do not use Flutter. Screen capture, hardware encoding, and system-level input hooks are implemented in Rust native modules—not Dart.

Normative sources: ADR-0007 · ADR-0003 · spec/frontend-toolchain-spec.md.

Common claims vs our view

Claim	Our view
“Flutter’s Skia/Impeller GPU rendering beats JS cross-platform”	Remote desktop bottlenecks are media pipelines and OS APIs, not self-drawn widget frame rates
“One Dart codebase for all platforms”	Capture/encode/hooks still need Rust/C++; splits from our TypeScript shared contracts and NestJS ecosystem
“Rspack is written in Rust too”	Rust powers build tools and runtime native modules—different roles; UI stays on React

Big frontend: React + Rspack toolchain

Surface	Runtime	Bundler
Web Client / Admin	React 19 + antd	Rsbuild (Rspack)
Desktop renderer	React + antd (aligned with Web)	Rsbuild
Mobile controller	React Native (New Architecture)	Metro
Docs site	MDX	Rspress

Electron: Chromium WebGL2 / WebGPU are production-ready; video uses WebRTC + hardware decode.

React Native: JSI gives near zero-copy paths to native code; legacy bridge latency is no longer the main issue for react-native-webrtc.

Native layer: Rust, not Dart

Examples of what remote desktop requires:

Windows DXGI Desktop Duplication capture

NVENC / QSV hardware encoding

System-level keyboard/mouse hooks

Zero-frame IPC with the Agent Service

Flutter/Dart cannot own these well. Rust ships as N-API modules for Electron and Native Module + JSI for RN—Rust engineers focus on AV/native performance; TS/React engineers own product UI.

See Desktop performance for the internal roadmap (no user-facing Rust schedule in docs).

UI cross-platform	React / RN + antd family	Dart widgets
Bundling	Rsbuild / Metro	Flutter toolchain
Native performance	Rust (ADR-0003)	Still needs C++/Rust plugins
Backend contracts	TypeScript shared	Extra bridging

title: Async jobs: why BullMQ
content:
VistaRemote uses BullMQ on Redis for AI audit, recording summaries, behavior reports, and other background work—not RabbitMQ or Kafka. This is an engineering choice for a TypeScript/NestJS team at sub–10M-scale throughput, not a log-aggregation platform.

Normative spec: job-queue-spec · ADR: 0006-bullmq-async-jobs.

vs real-time messaging

Kind	Stack	Purpose
Signaling / notifications	WebSocket, SSE, DataChannel	Low latency
Background jobs	BullMQ + Redis	Delay, retry, observable state

See Messaging & transport.

1. NestJS / TypeScript ecosystem

BullMQ is the most capable and actively maintained distributed job queue in Node.js, with first-class @nestjs/bullmq:

Producers (server): @InjectQueue, queue.add(...) with DI

Consumers (ai): @Processor / @Process, idiomatic NestJS

RabbitMQ (amqplib) and Kafka (kafkajs) require substantial custom connection, reconnect, and flow-control code.

2. AI audit needs job semantics, not log streams

AI audit differs from log shipping:

LLM calls often take hundreds of ms to seconds

Rate limits require delayed retry and exponential backoff

Admins need per-job states: Waiting, Active, Completed, Failed, Delayed

BullMQ tracks per-job lifecycle in Redis. Kafka is a log stream without native single-job delay/backoff. RabbitMQ needs DLX/DLQ-heavy custom patterns.

3. Operations: reuse Redis

Redis is already required for sessions, signaling fan-out, and SSE. BullMQ adds no new broker. A small Redis instance is enough for high-throughput queues at our scale.

Kafka is operationally heavy (KRaft/ZK, disk I/O) and impractical on 1 vCPU / 2 GB VMs for this product class.

4. Data path is simple and denoised

Agents filter frames and desensitize locally; the cloud receives structured behavior events, not raw frame floods. Routing is linear:

Agent → server enqueue → ai worker

No RabbitMQ-style exchange topology.

5. Summary

Dimension	BullMQ + Redis	Kafka	RabbitMQ
NestJS DX	✅ Official module	⚠️ Custom	⚠️ Custom
Per-job delay/backoff	✅ Built-in	❌ DIY	⚠️ Partial
Job state	✅	❌	⚠️
Extra infra	None	Cluster	Broker
Fit for VistaRemote	✅ AI jobs	Log pipes	Complex routing

Smooth remote control	WebRTC + client-side GPU encode + optional Rust for DXGI/NVENC

For executives and business owners

Spend on outcomes, not two stacks

Flutter’s pitch is “one UI codebase.” For remote desktop, capture, hardware encode, and global input hooks are not Dart problems — you still need Rust/C++ engineers.

VistaRemote uses React for product UI and Rust only where it matters. Fewer surprises in budget and timeline.

Delivery speed is a competitive edge

Meta-Repo multi-repo: clone only web + server for a demo.

Rspack/Rsbuild: Rust-powered bundling — hundreds of ms cold starts.

Spec-driven development: requirements trace to FR IDs.

Data stays on your infrastructure

Recordings, audit logs, and AI summaries can run entirely in your VPC — a strong story vs closed monitoring vendors.

For IT and operations

Familiar, small footprint

P2P + TURN (default)

Fetch ICE from GET /api/v1/ice/servers.

Two or more controllers in a room

coturn load ratio exceeds threshold

Enterprise forceSfu

title: WebRTC topology
content:
VistaRemote defaults to P2P + STUN/TURN (coturn) for 1:1 remote desktop. Use mediasoup SFU when multiple controllers watch one agent, P2P keeps failing, or TURN relay load is too high.

Commercial: SFU is included during the 7-day standard_7d trial; after trial you need Pro or higher. See Trial and paid features.

Normative spec: Meta-Repo spec/webrtc-architecture-spec.md

Use case	Remote desktop & enterprise monitoring, not mass live streaming
Scale	Tens of concurrent sessions — mediasoup sidecar is enough
Stack	TypeScript end-to-end, same ops model as server/ai
Cost	SRS adds a separate C++ media plane we do not need

Mode matrix

Scenario	Mode	Media path
1 controller : 1 agent	P2P	End-to-end; coturn relay if needed
1 agent : N controllers	SFU	Single uplink to mediasoup; N downlinks
Repeated ICE failure	SFU	Server policy fallback
coturn overload	SFU	New sessions prefer SFU to spare TURN

Channels

Channel	Purpose
RTP	Screen video
DataChannel control	Input events
WebSocket	Signaling only

title: Docker Deployment
content:
Layered Compose stack in the deploy repo (MetaRepo sibling: deploy/ at the repo root). Spec: deploy-spec (FR-STD-01 … FR-STD-07).

Layers

File	Role
compose/docker-compose.core.yml	server + PostgreSQL + Redis (required baseline)
compose/docker-compose.dev.yml	Local host ports; optional profiles
compose/docker-compose.prod.yml	Caddy TLS; no DB/Redis on the host
compose/docker-compose.external-db.yml	Managed Postgres/Redis instead of bundled containers
compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml	Entitlement :3040 + OIDC (no IdP container)

Root docker-compose.yml is a convenience include of core + dev — prefer explicit -f flags in runbooks.

Local (core + dev)

cd deploy
cp compose/.env.example .env    # or --env-file compose/.env.example

docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f compose/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d

Service	Host port	Notes
postgres	5637	PostgreSQL 16 — only relational OLTP (LuminaryWorks default)
redis	6380	Sessions, BullMQ
server	3000	NestJS API + signaling

Optional services use profiles on the dev overlay (opt-in; lab publishers stay off by default):

Profile	Services	Host ports
turn	coturn	3478/5349, relay 49160–49200/udp
ai	Ollama, Qdrant, python-worker	11435, 6335, 4100 — see Local AI dev
recording	MinIO	API 19000, console 19001
admin	static admin (Caddy)	8081
edge	Caddy 80/443	dev TLS edge

# examples
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f compose/docker-compose.dev.yml --profile turn up -d
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f compose/docker-compose.dev.yml --profile recording up -d

From the MetaRepo root (equivalent paths):

docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d

More detail: deploy/README.md in the deploy-stack repo (or MetaRepo deploy/README.md).

Recording (MinIO)

Phase 1 desktop recording uses the dev overlay recording profile (MinIO). The default production stack has no MinIO — set OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT to external S3 in .env.prod.

docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f compose/docker-compose.dev.yml --profile recording up -d

Caller	Endpoint	Notes
server (in compose)	http://minio:9000	Docker-internal DNS
Desktop Agent (on host)	http://127.0.0.1:19000	Presigned URLs must be host-reachable
MinIO Console	http://127.0.0.1:19001	Create the bucket if needed

Bucket: vistaremote-recordings. Desktop OBJECT_STORAGE_* must match MINIO_ROOT_USER / MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD; set OBJECT_STORAGE_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true.

Without the profile — unit tests or local dev without MinIO: OBJECT_STORAGE_DRIVER=memory (no compose profile).

Part size — Desktop coalesces non-final parts to ≥5 MiB before multipart PUT (S3/MinIO return EntityTooSmall otherwise); the final part may be smaller. With memory, the server still accepts small parts via /parts. Ops hints: Admin console · FAQ.

Production

Use core + prod (non-SFU baseline; optional --profile turn only when this host runs VistaRemote coturn).

cd deploy
cp compose/.env.prod.example compose/.env.prod
# edit DOMAIN, secrets, TURN_EXTERNAL_IP
pnpm assert:prod-env

docker compose --env-file compose/.env.prod \
  -f compose/docker-compose.core.yml -f compose/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build

Do not publish Postgres or Redis on the host in production. The default prod stack has no MinIO recording profile — use external S3 for recordings. Full DNS, firewall, health checks, backup, and rollback steps → MetaRepo v1 Go-Live checklist (plan/v1-golive-checklist.md).

pnpm assert:prod-env

Run from deploy/ after editing compose/.env.prod, before docker compose up. Read-only checks; exits 1 on failure without modifying files.

Target	What is checked
compose/.env.prod.example (always)	File exists; required keys present: DOMAIN, DB_PASSWORD, three VISTAREMOTE_*_JWT_SECRET, VISTAREMOTE_ADMIN_PASSWORD, TURN_USERNAME_PREFIX=vr:, TURN_REALM, ENTITLEMENT_MODE / ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL / ENTITLEMENT_SERVICE_API_KEY / ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET, INTERVENTION_HMAC_KEYS / INTERVENTION_MAX_SKEW_SEC / INTERVENTION_LINK_TTL_SEC; ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL must include :3040 (retired 7090 is rejected)
compose/.env.prod (if present)	Rejects weak placeholders: CHANGE_ME, vistaremote, miniosecret, password / admin / 123456, dev-* JWTs, host.docker.internal; requires TURN_USERNAME_PREFIX=vr:; when Entitlement is on, ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL should target :3040; with ENTITLEMENT_MODE=enforce, ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET must be non-empty (empty → inbound webhook always 401)
compose/.env.prod (if missing)	Example-only pass with WARN … example checked only

CHANGE_ME_* in the example is documentation-only; your real compose/.env.prod must use strong secrets. Passing this check does not mean a production payment PSP is shipped — see the Go-Live checklist and deploy/README.md for sandbox credentials.

Shared TURN

If VistaCast already binds 3478/5349, do not enable --profile turn. Point server env at the existing instance: TURN_URL, TURN_REALM=turn.vistaremote.<domain>, TURN_USERNAME_PREFIX=vr:.

title: CI/CD and versioning
content:
VistaRemote uses per-repository builds and releases: each sub-repo has its own SemVer tags and GitHub Actions workflows. When @vistaremote/shared is published, downstream repos are notified to bump their dependency.

Full normative spec: Meta-Repo spec/cicd-release-spec.md

Version and tag conventions

Repo	Tag format	Example	Artifact
shared	vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH	v0.2.0	npm @vistaremote/shared (GitHub Packages)
server	server-v*	server-v0.2.0	Docker ghcr.io/vistaremote/server
ai	ai-v*	ai-v0.2.0	Docker ghcr.io/vistaremote/ai
web	web-v*	web-v0.2.0	Static artifacts (client + admin)
desktop	desktop-v*	desktop-v0.2.0	Build artifact (installers P1)
docs	docs-v*	docs-v0.2.0	GitHub Pages
deploy	deploy-v*	deploy-v0.2.0	Compose validation / release notes
mobile	mobile-v*	mobile-v0.2.0	Build verification (stores P1)
downloads (public)	v*	v1.0.0	Windows Agent + Android APK (anonymous download)

Tags are the source of truth for releases; keep package.json#version aligned when possible.

End-user installers (public bucket)

desktop / mobile source may stay private. User-facing binaries are published to the public repo VistaRemote/downloads. The marketing site /download page defaults to that repo’s releases/latest/download.

From the Meta-Repo:

pnpm pack:publish          # pack:all + upload to VistaRemote/downloads Release
pnpm publish:downloads     # upload existing artifacts only

Requires gh auth login and matching desktop / mobile package versions. Prefer building the Windows Agent on Windows or via the desktop Actions workflow (windows-latest); Android APK can be built on macOS with pnpm pack:mobile.

Website defaults:

NEXT_PUBLIC_RELEASE_BASE=https://github.com/VistaRemote/downloads/releases/latest/download

NEXT_PUBLIC_RELEASE_VERSION=1.0.0 (must match asset filenames)

Recommended release order

1. Merge shared to main
2. Tag v0.2.0 → release.yml publishes npm package
3. repository_dispatch → consumer sync-shared.yml opens PRs
4. Merge bump PRs, tag server-v0.2.0 / web-v0.2.0 / …
5. Update deploy compose image tags → deploy-v0.2.0

Publish shared

cd shared
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin v0.2.0

Workflow shared/.github/workflows/release.yml: lint → test → build → publish → notify consumers.

Consumer auto-bump

sync-shared.yml on each consumer:

Sets @vistaremote/shared to ^0.2.0

Runs install, lint, test, build

Opens PR: chore(deps): bump @vistaremote/shared to 0.2.0

Release services

cd server
git tag server-v0.2.0
git push origin server-v0.2.0

Local vs CI vs production

Environment	@vistaremote/shared
Meta-Repo dev	file:../shared in package.json
GitHub Actions	setup-shared composite action (sibling checkout)
Docker / offline	GitHub Packages pinned SemVer

Restore local file: deps after a registry bump:

node tooling/scripts/restore-shared-file-deps.mjs

CI workflows

Workflow	Trigger	Purpose
ci.yml	push / PR	setup-shared → lint → test → build
sync-shared.yml	shared-published	Auto bump + PR
release.yml	tag	Images / static site / npm
dependency-review.yml	PR	Dependency review
CodeQL	push / PR	Security analysis

Meta-Repo meta-ci.yml only checks scaffolding, not sub-repo app code.

Maintainer setup

Secret on VistaRemote/shared: VISTAREMOTE_CI_PAT (repo + workflow) for cross-repo dispatch.

Sync workflow templates from Meta-Repo root:

node tooling/scripts/setup-github-workflows.mjs

title: Linux logged-in remote control (portal and X11)
content:
VistaRemote does not require turning Wayland off or forcing Xorg. A logged-in graphical session is enough.

Session types

Environment	Input inject	Capture (this iteration)
X11 (DISPLAY only)	XTest	Chromium getDisplayMedia
XWayland (WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY)	XTest first	Screen-share portal / Chromium
Pure Wayland (WAYLAND_DISPLAY only)	xdg-desktop-portal RemoteDesktop; otherwise CONTROL_NEEDS_PORTAL	Screen-share portal

The Agent never silently drops pointer/keyboard events. Controllers see CONTROL_NEEDS_PORTAL in diagnostics when the portal is required.

Lab: VR_WAYLAND_PORTAL=live (W14-B)

For development / lab (not production sign-off):

Value	Use
mock	In-process grant/deny without D-Bus (CI/unit tests)
live	Force live: filesystem-probe xdg-desktop-portal + libei, then Agent RemoteDesktop
auto	Default; same probe path on pure Wayland
off	Always CONTROL_NEEDS_PORTAL on pure Wayland

Missing xdg-desktop-portal / libei yields an honest CONTROL_NEEDS_PORTAL (reasons: portal-missing / libei-missing / portal-deps-missing) — never a silent inject success. X11 / XWayland stay on XTest. Full lab steps: Meta-Repo plan/wayland-live-lab.md.

Ubuntu GNOME (Wayland) consent

Start the Desktop Agent and connect from a controller.

Approve the Screen sharing portal and pick a display.

For inject, approve the Remote Desktop (or input devices) portal — pointer and keyboard.

Keep the permission for the session under Settings → Privacy → Screen Sharing.

If no dialog appears, install xdg-desktop-portal and xdg-desktop-portal-gnome, then log out and retry.

KDE Plasma uses the KDE desktop portal (“Remote control”).

Headless/minimal images without a portal should run the Agent in an X11 session, or keep XWayland DISPLAY.

Out of scope

Distro defaults such as WaylandEnable=false

Display manager / GDM / lock-screen inject

Root uinput as the default path

VistaRemote uses a core + plugins model. Contracts live in @vistaremote/shared (Manifest, permissions, apiVersion). This guide covers the scaffold CLI only — signing, marketplace, and dynamic install into production Agents are not shipped yet.

See Spec: plugin-architecture-spec.

Local Meta-Repo with pnpm --dir shared build

Node.js ≥ 24

CLI (tooling/vt-cli)

pnpm vt-cli create plugin --id com.acme.demo --name "Demo" --targets server,web

# Validate Manifest (shared validatePluginManifest)
pnpm vt-cli validate ./demo

# Pack (unsigned)
pnpm vt-cli pack ./demo --format zip
pnpm vt-cli pack ./demo --format tgz

The scaffold includes plugin.manifest.json, per-target placeholders, and Biome config.

Minimal Manifest fields

Field	Notes
id	Reverse-domain, e.g. com.acme.demo
name / version	Display name and semver
apiVersion	Currently vistaremote-host/1
targets	server | web | desktop | mobile
permissions	e.g. ui.overlay (must be a known shared permission)
entry	Per-target entry paths
publisher	{ name } (public-key fingerprint comes with signing later)

Limits

No ed25519 signing

No vt publish / plugin-index market

Hosts still load the in-process hello Manifest; archives are not dynamically installed into production Agents

title: Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
content:
VistaRemote iterates with Specs as the boundary: requirement IDs and acceptance criteria first, then code.

Canonical spec: Meta-Repo spec/spec-driven-development-spec.md.

Document layers

Layer	Location	Audience
L0	system-overview.md	User stories US-xx
L1	*-spec.md	Module FR-xx
L2	server/spec/SPEC.md etc.	Single-repo detail
End users	This site user/*	Operators & end users
Developers	This site guide/*	Contributors

Requirement IDs

Prefix	Meaning
US-xx	User story
FR-xxx	Functional requirement
SEC-xx	Security

List affected FRs in PR descriptions; refactors with no behavior change should say so explicitly.

Implementation order (required)

shared → server / ai → web | desktop | mobile → docs

Skipping this order causes contract drift and CI failures.

Implementation status

Before coding, read Implementation status:

✅ Ready: implement FRs as written

🟡 Partial: extend existing placeholder / in-memory stores

⬜ Planned: land infrastructure first or split a P1 task

PR checklist

Updated or confirmed relevant spec/*.md

Cross-platform changes in shared

Updated implementation-status.md when readiness changes

User-visible changes documented under user/* or guide/*

1.52.0 current viewer Admin (routed modules only)

Current apps/admin routes: Overview, Users, Devices, Orders, Sessions, Recordings, Permissions, Audit, System. Modules that may exist in historical Admin / API but are not mounted in the current viewer UI: Membership, Pairings, Organizations, Jobs, efficiency reports, monitor wall, security events.

Access

URL is typically https://<your-domain>/admin (provided by your operator)

Sign in with a platform admin or org admin account

Modules

Module	Purpose
Overview	Live count cards, including org count and pending orders, plus users, sessions, recordings, devices / online devices, and similar. /system is mounted (entitlement flags). Historical deep-links to /security, /monitor-wall, and Pairings NavCard → /pairings (1.41.0) may be unavailable in the current viewer build (see 1.52 note above)
Users	View / filter (including user ID and org ID) / create / disable accounts; assign org and plan; detail drawer related links (Sessions / Recordings / Pairings / Orders / Devices / Audit, 1.38.0; 1.42.0 adds Pairings); export CSV
Devices	Agent online status (heartbeat within about 120 seconds), online / offline, owner / org, and label filters, label edit, revoke device; Pairings in Actions → /pairings?deviceId= (1.41.0); Monitor wall in Actions when the device has an active session (s0 seed, 1.38.0); export CSV (overview Online devices deep-links to the online filter)
Pairings	Read-only recent pairing codes from PostgreSQL (FR-WAD-109, 1.39.0); filter by device ID, owner user ID, numeric code, and consumed (yes = consumedAt set, no = unused — URL-synced, 1.41.0); row Device / User / Session links to /devices?deviceId=, /users?userId=, /sessions?sessionId= (1.40.0 session deep-link); page header Create audit / Join audit → `/audit?action=pairing.create	join(**1.44.0**); pairing **policy** (length / TTL) on **System**, with **Open pairings** →/pairings` in the policy section
Sessions	Active remote rooms (p2p / SFU); admins can force disconnect / observe (single stream; 1.36.0 observe ticket = shared AdminObserveTicket); filter by user ID (?userId= URL-synced, 1.38.0); export CSV
Recordings	Filter by user, recording ID, device ID, status, session, and trigger; export CSV; EntityTooSmall / part-size hints on failed rows (banner + tooltips; ≥5 MiB coalesce); built-in player fetches a playback-url short-lived signed stream (expiresAt, refresh on expiry; in-memory /media); seek and playback speed
Audit	Filter by actor, action presets (including observe / SupportGrant / operator and member roles, pairing.create / pairing.join (1.43.0), and monitor-wall layout), time, resource / resource type, and result (ok / denied / error); admin.monitor_wall.layout rows link Monitor wall (meta roomIds / roomId → ?s0=, slot seed only, 1.38.0); export CSV
Security events	Exfiltration risk, bulk delete, behavior inference, and similar; filter by type, deviceId, userId, and orgId; editable alert rules lite (banner min severity + muted types; not a correlation engine); list applies saved mute rules by default (Switch Apply mute rules; applyMute=false or URL ?applyMute=false shows all types); high-severity banner; jump to a related recording timestamp / session / device; export CSV
Organizations	Orgs, seats/members, and policy (keywords, domains, and similar); change member orgRole; drawer SupportGrant (IT-assist) create / list / revoke / export CSV (optional Revoke and disconnect related sessions, ?kickSessions=true); list CSV; detail members CSV
Orders	Filter plan orders by user, SKU, provider, source, and status. The list can show local billing and commerce mirror rows. Simulate paid appears only on source=local_billing pending rows and calls POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/simulate-paid. Commerce rows have no button; the API returns 400 COMMERCE_SIMULATE_PAID_FORBIDDEN (use Client Membership complete / webhook). Production without BILLING_ALLOW_SIMULATE_PAID returns 400 SIMULATE_PAID_DISABLED. Do not use an Admin JWT against /billing/.../simulate-paid. Page copy: WeChat / Alipay production notify is on Entitlement, not this page. Historical row Membership → /membership?userId=… has no Admin Membership route in the current viewer
Membership	Checkout is Web Client /membership (current viewer Admin has no such route): trial countdown, legal, SKU, catalog providerHint (wechat / alipay), QR / codeUrl / redirect; after pay, status polling + complete refreshes entitlements. On-page sandbox copy is not production PSP. Historical Admin Membership (?userId=, Open orders) is unrouted
System	FR-WAD-52 entitlement/payment config flags (read-only): entitlementMode, entitlementBaseUrlConfigured, webhookSecretConfigured; Copy entitlement status JSON. Never exposes secrets or Base URL plaintext. Enforce readiness ≠ live WeChat/Alipay merchant
Jobs	Background jobs (for example recording summaries): list; filter by id / name / state / failedReason (URL-synced; overview failed jobs → ?state=failed); recording.summarize rows link to Recordings; retry failed jobs; export CSV
Efficiency reports	Weekly / monthly recording-minute totals; filter by userId / sessionId / deviceId / recordingId before rollup (from recording metadata, not an LLM efficiency model); Open recordings deep-link with active filters; export CSV
Permissions	Platform / org permission matrices are read-only; export reference CSV; assign platform operator roles (not checkbox Permission edits)

Common tasks

Grant Pro to a user

Closed trial preferred: Admin Users → change plan (writes local User.plan immediately).

Sandbox checkout: the user opens Web Client /membership, picks providerHint (WeChat / Alipay), then waits for polling or clicks Complete payment. That is not live merchant notify.

Local pending orders only: Admin Orders Simulate paid (POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/simulate-paid). The order owner may also call /api/v1/billing/orders/:id/simulate-paid with a Controller JWT. Commerce orders return COMMERCE_SIMULATE_PAID_FORBIDDEN.

Entitlements apply after the user refreshes the client or signs in again.

Disable a user

Users → select user → disable.

The user cannot start new sessions. For an active session, open Sessions and force disconnect.

Monitor wall layout

Product capability (Enterprise): multi-device thumbnail observe; click into high-quality remote control when needed. Larger slot counts can be purchased and accepted under enterprise contracts. See Device Fleet & Enterprise.

Ops quick steps:

Open /monitor-wall and bind active sessions to slots.

Save layout (requires admin.write) to persist bindings.

URL seeds such as s0–s3 can prefill slots.

Click a live slot to open a control session (enterprise wall / remote entitlements required).

(Version history and API notes below remain for implementers.)

Layout persistence (1.35.0) — persists slot-to-session bindings.

Open /monitor-wall. URL query s0–s3 (aliases slot0–slot3 accepted) with session IDs take priority and are not overwritten by a saved layout.

With no URL seeds, the page GETs /admin/monitor-wall/layout to restore the last saved slot bindings.

After changing slots, click Save layout to PUT the same path (requires admin.write; read-only admins see the button disabled). Saving the layout does not auto-start in-wall observe or SFU connections.

Per-slot in-wall observe provides thumbnail observe; click a live slot for high-quality control when needed. Enterprise multi-screen wall scale: Device Fleet & Enterprise.

1.36.0 — POST /admin/rooms/:roomId/observe returns shared AdminObserveTicket (signalingTicket, role: observe, expiresAt, …). SFU observe parameters are issued by the server.

1.37.0 / 1.38.0 — Filter audit by action preset monitor-wall layout (admin.monitor_wall.layout). 1.38.0 — Save layout writes audit meta with roomIds (bound session ids) and the first roomId. Matching rows show Monitor wall in Related → /monitor-wall, or /monitor-wall?s0=<roomId> from meta / resource / target roomId / room_id. Slot 0 seed only; start observe from the wall when needed.

1.44.0 — Page tips cover layout save and in-wall / enterprise multi-screen observe.

Jobs, reports, and recordings (1.37.0)

Jobs — List filters (id, name, state, failedReason) sync to the URL when you search (shareable links; overview failed jobs opens /jobs?state=failed).

Recording summarize jobs — Rows with type recording.summarize and id summarize-{recordingId} show Recording in Actions, linking to /recordings?recordingId=… (other job types have no recording jump).

Efficiency reports — Open recordings opens /recordings with the same active substring filters (userId, sessionId, deviceId, recordingId); empty filters open the full list.

Pairings list (1.39.0 / 1.40.0 / 1.41.0)

FR-WAD-109 — read-only ops view of recent pairing codes; not a code generator or SFU / monitor-wall feature.

Open /pairings under Operations (nav between Devices and Orders), from Overview → Pairings NavCard (1.41.0), from Devices → Actions → Pairings (?deviceId= pre-filled, 1.41.0), or from System → pairing-policy section Open pairings (1.40.0).

The page calls GET /api/v1/admin/pairings (requires admin.read). Default returns up to 100 recent rows; optional query limit is clamped 1–500.

Server filters: deviceId and numericCode (substring, case-insensitive); userId filters by the device owner resolved from the devices table; consumed (1.41.0) — yes = consumedAt set (code already used), no = consumedAt null (unused); unknown values are ignored.

Search fields sync to ?deviceId=, ?userId=, ?numericCode=, and ?consumed=yes|no in the URL (shareable links). The Consumed select offers Consumed / Unused / All.

Columns include numeric code, deviceId, userId (owner), sessionId, expiresAt, consumedAt. In Actions, Device → /devices?deviceId=…; User → /users?userId=… when an owner is known; Session → /sessions?sessionId=… (1.40.0, when the row has sessionId; Sessions filter syncs to ?sessionId= in the URL).

To change code length or TTL, use System pairing policy; hosts still generate codes on the Agent.

1.44.0 — Page header Create audit / Join audit open /audit?action=pairing.create or pairing.join (same presets as the Audit action filter since 1.43.0).

User drawer and cross-module links (1.38.0 / 1.42.0)

Users — In the detail drawer, View sessions / recordings / pairings / orders / devices / audit deep-link to /sessions?userId=…, /recordings?userId=…, /pairings?userId=… (1.42.0; Pairings list filters by device owner substring), /orders?userId=…, /devices?ownerId=…, and /audit?actorId=… (devices list filters by ownerId; the drawer device tab still uses owner / org logic).

Devices — When a row has an active session (correlated with in-memory rooms), Actions shows Monitor wall → /monitor-wall?s0=<sessionId> (slot 0 seed; not SFU multi-stream shipped).

Sessions — Filter by user ID; filters sync to ?userId= in the URL (the user drawer View sessions button seeds this param). Client-side filter matches row userId (rows without userId do not match).

Membership and orders (1.42.0 / 1.43.0 / 1.52.0)

Checkout — Web Client /membership (current viewer Admin has no Membership route): providerHint, QR/redirect, status polling after pay, and Complete payment (complete). Sandbox copy is not production PSP.

Orders — Admin Orders lists local rows; Simulate paid is local_billing pending only. Read commerce together with Client Membership. Historical Admin Membership↔Orders deep-links are unrouted in the current viewer.

Grant — If a trial user is stuck on Free, prefer Users → change plan; do not simulate-pay commerce orders.

Enterprise enablement & contract scope

These capabilities are under Enterprise Fleet / contract scope (see Device Fleet & Enterprise) and are delivered per enablement and contract:

An editable permission matrix (the Permissions page is a read-only reference; role enablement is configured during rollout)

Larger-slot / multi-screen monitor wall scale (default in-wall observe; add-ons in the Fleet guide)

A correlation engine or alert DSL (alert rules lite is banner threshold + mute types)

Production WeChat Pay / Alipay secrets (never commit them; configure via Entitlement / environment)

Engineering readiness: Implementation status.

Security

Prefer VPN or a private network for the admin URL; MFA is planned (P1).

Audit sensitive actions (disable user, plan changes, force disconnect, device revoke); filter and export CSV as needed.

Ops FAQ

Mute rules, SupportGrant, entitlement flags, recording EntityTooSmall, monitor wall, user drawer links, jobs/reports recording jumps, audit layout → monitor wall, pairings list, consumed filter, Overview/Devices entry points, session deep-links, Users→Pairings, Membership↔Orders, pairing audit presets, Forbidden dashboard, and Pairings→Audit header: FAQ § Admin & remote ops.

Developers: Admin getting started.

Payments and Entitlement (mock → sandbox)

Mode	Behavior
ENTITLEMENT_MODE=off (default)	Local plan/orders; no central Entitlement
ENTITLEMENT_MODE=enforce	Entitlement is authoritative for commercial checkout
Mock / dev	Owner POST /api/v1/billing/orders/:id/simulate-paid; Admin POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/simulate-paid (local_billing only)
Sandbox WeChat / Alipay	Client /membership: providerHint wechat→wechat_pay_v3, alipay→alipay_f2f; poll status + complete; secrets only in Entitlement

title: AI assist (Windows / macOS computer use)
content:
AI assist is off unless you turn it on. After that, you can type one task in Viewer and let your organization's AI click and type in windows that are already open on the remote Windows or macOS Agent, including the browser.

The tool surface matches open-source Windows-MCP and MacOS-MCP-style look → click/type computer use. VistaRemote does not bundle those programs. By default it maps the same allowed steps onto the existing WebRTC DataChannel so AI and human control share one path. An optional Agent setting can start windows-mcp or macos-mcp on local stdio and, if that process fails, falls back to the same input path.

This is not unattended takeover. It does not run scripts, edit the registry, or write files.

Why this is a core capability

VistaRemote AI assist	Typical desktop MCP (Windows-MCP / MacOS-MCP)
Target	Remote Windows / macOS Agent	Local desktop
Tools	Bounded observe, Click, Type, scroll	Same look → click/type idea
Transport	Live remote session + private AI Worker	Local MCP host
Consent	Separate "Allow AI" after human control consent	Host trust model
Default	Off; alerts never auto-arm control	Host-defined

Use it to help a colleague open a settings page, fill a form in their browser, or walk through recovery — not to run scripts or edit the registry from Viewer.

Before you start

The Agent is installed (Windows or macOS) and you are already in a session together.

The host taps Allow. That only allows a person to use the keyboard and mouse.

If this Agent has AI assist enabled, the host sees a second prompt. AI does not move the pointer until they tap Allow AI. The Viewer toolbar shows AI assist only after the server has the feature on.

A small snapshot of the screen goes to your own AI service so it can choose the next click. This feature does not add a public model key.

How to use it

Open AI assist from the Viewer toolbar. Human chat stays on its own button.

Write the task, for example "click the browser address bar". An empty task does not start.

The step list shows tool names such as Click or Type.

Press Stop, or move the mouse or keyboard yourself. The AI pauses. Your own control works as before.

One task stops after about 20 steps or 3 minutes.

Local AI (Cursor / ChatGPT)

A local MCP process can operate a session you have already joined, after the remote host has allowed AI. It cannot open a new remote session. If the server flag is off, the tools return COPILOT_DISABLED.

Use the same command for ChatGPT desktop when it can launch a local stdio MCP. Do not put a real ticket in git. The example is tooling/mcp/cursor-mcp.example.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vista-remote": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "tooling/mcp/vista-remote-mcp.mjs"
      ],
      "env": {
        "VR_API_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:3000",
        "VR_SIGNALING_TICKET": "<signaling-ticket-for-an-existing-session>",
        "VR_SESSION_ID": "<session-id>"
      }
    }
  }
}

Tools are vr_snapshot, vr_click, vr_type, vr_scroll, vr_move, vr_shortcut, and vr_wait. PowerShell, shell, and the ecosystem remote_control handoff tool are not in this list.

Not in this version

Whether a click lands on a real Windows or macOS desktop still needs a person to look. This page does not call the feature production-signed.

It does not lock the screen, sign out, run PowerShell or a shell, or edit the registry.

An alert does not start a remote session or this assist by itself.

The same AI action is not broadcast to a group of computers.

title: FAQ (Users)
content:
Pairing & connection

Invalid pairing code?
It may have expired (~5 minutes by default), been mistyped, or already consumed (PAIRING_CONSUMED — a class cannot share one code); regenerate on the host.

Video works but no control?
Confirm the host Agent clicked Allow, and pairing was not View only. The control channel may also be missing. Mouse/keyboard inject exists on Windows and macOS. Refresh the session or check Agent version with IT.

Stuck on connecting?
Check network/firewall UDP and whether TURN is configured.

Is VistaRemote MeshCentral?
No. VistaRemote is WebRTC remote control plus an enterprise device fleet (group control, monitor wall, virtual display, and more — see Device Fleet & Enterprise). Out-of-band AMT is an enterprise private-deploy contract capability. Registry, remote print, and login-window injection are out of scope. Comparison: Product comparison.

Do you have group control / monitor wall / virtual display?
Yes — Enterprise product capabilities. Enable after purchasing enterprise service; larger wall slots and site customizations follow the contract. See Device Fleet & Enterprise.

Plans

Cannot multi-view after trial?
SFU requires Pro/Enterprise — see Plans & billing.

Is device fleet sold separately?
Group control, monitor wall, virtual display, and OOB ship under Enterprise (plus contract add-ons). Endpoint management can be priced per device / seat — see Plans & billing and your sales proposal.

Can I use the open-source build commercially?
Free for personal non-commercial use; all commercial use requires a paid license — see Licensing.

Privacy & AI

Is data sent to OpenAI by default?
Default private deployment uses Ollama + self-hosted vector DB; cloud inference only when enabled and entitled.

What does Desktop AI do?
Local rules/light inference for behavior hints; heavy jobs go to the ai worker queue.

Admin & remote ops

How do I force-disconnect a session?
Open the Admin console → Sessions and force disconnect the active room. The server closes the signaling WebSocket first, then clears the in-memory room. The host can also disconnect from the always-on-top connection bar; see Remote control. Disabling a user does not kick an in-progress session — still disconnect it under Sessions.

When is a device “online”? What are labels?
Online means the device’s last heartbeat was within about 120 seconds; after that it is offline. Online is not “currently sharing the screen.” On Devices you can edit labels and filter by them. Revoking a device makes the next heartbeat fail; that is separate from the online check. See Admin console.

How does recording playback work? Is it a MinIO player?
No. Playback is a local browser <video> on the Recordings page (seek / speed), not a MinIO product player. Desktop MediaRecorder multipart upload and MinIO storage ship with the dev recording profile — see Docker deployment.

ICE stuck — should I change DNS?
Do not start by changing DNS. ICE candidates come from the Server. Admin System shows entitlement flags (FR-WAD-52). If it still fails, check UDP/firewall and TURN; see Remote control connection quality.

Can I edit the permission matrix?
No. The Permissions page is a read-only map of platform RBAC / org roles. Role and permission enablement is configured by enterprise rollout / platform admins per org policy. See Admin console.

How do Admin CSV exports work?
They export the currently filtered/loaded list (client-side unless the page says otherwise; audit CSV is server-filtered, including result). Users, devices, security, jobs, orders, orgs, and recordings have CSV buttons where implemented; the org drawer SupportGrant table also has export grants CSV (1.33.0). This is not a full warehouse dump, and not a billing/payment export. See Admin console.

Can I open overview cards and list filters from a URL?
Yes. Overview metric cards and most list filters support URL query seeds (for example /devices?online=offline, /users?planExpiry=expired, /audit?result=denied, /recordings?status=failed). Permission matrix search is a read-only filter, not editable roles. See Admin console.

How do security mute rules work?
On Admin console → Security events, configure muted types (alert rules lite). The list applies saved rules by default (Switch Apply mute rules); turn it off or open ?applyMute=false to see all types. The high-severity banner count still excludes muted types.

Where is SupportGrant managed? Does revoke kick sessions?
In the organization drawer: create / list / revoke SupportGrant temporary IT-assist grants, and export grants CSV (current filter/loaded rows). The revoke confirmation can check Revoke and disconnect related sessions (?kickSessions=true, off by default). The permission matrix stays read-only. See Admin console.

What are the System page entitlement flags?
Admin System shows read-only entitlementMode, entitlementBaseUrlConfigured, and webhookSecretConfigured (GET /api/v1/admin/system/entitlement, FR-WAD-52) — no secrets. Copy entitlement status JSON to verify; it is not a plan-grant UI. See Admin console. Production webhook / simulate-paid checks: Production payment readiness.

Recording playback URL expired? MinIO EntityTooSmall?
The Recordings player fetches a short-lived signed playback-url (expiresAt; refresh on expiry). When failedReason matches EntityTooSmall / part size, the list shows a hint that the Agent should coalesce non-final parts to ≥5 MiB (Desktop ≥1.30; memory:// still allows small parts). See Admin console.

What is the monitor wall, and how do we enable it?
The monitor wall is an Enterprise multi-screen observe capability: low-cost thumbnail observe across devices, then click into high-quality remote control when needed. Larger slot counts can be added under the enterprise contract. See Device Fleet & Enterprise and Admin console.

What does the observe ticket return?
When Admin starts observe on a room, the server returns an observe ticket (signaling and SFU-related parameters) for in-wall or observe pull. See Admin console.

Does the monitor wall layout save automatically?
No. URL s0–s3 take priority; without seeds the page restores from GET /admin/monitor-wall/layout; click Save layout (PUT, admin.write) to persist. See Admin console.

How do I open a recording from a summarize job (1.37.0)?
On Jobs, recording.summarize rows with id summarize-{recordingId} show Recording in Actions → /recordings?recordingId=…. Job filters (id, name, state, failedReason) sync to the URL; overview failed jobs opens /jobs?state=failed.

How do efficiency reports open the recordings list (1.37.0)?
On Efficiency reports, click Open recordings — it carries active userId / sessionId / deviceId / recordingId substring filters to /recordings (rollup period is not passed; filters only).

Audit layout rows and monitor wall (1.37.0 / 1.38.0)?
Filter audit by monitor-wall layout (admin.monitor_wall.layout). 1.38.0 — Save layout audit meta includes roomIds and the first roomId. Matching rows show Monitor wall — /monitor-wall or /monitor-wall?s0=<roomId> from meta / resource / target roomId / room_id. Slot 0 seed only; open observe from the wall when needed. See Admin console.

How do user drawer related links work (1.38.0)?
On Users, open the detail drawer and click View sessions / recordings / orders / devices / audit — they open /sessions?userId=…, /recordings?userId=…, /orders?userId=…, /devices?ownerId=…, and /audit?actorId=…. See Admin console.

How do I jump to the monitor wall from an active device session (1.38.0)?
On Devices, when a row has an active session, Actions shows Monitor wall → /monitor-wall?s0=<sessionId>. This seeds slot 0; start in-wall observe from the wall when needed. See Admin console.

How do I filter sessions by user ID (1.38.0)?
On Sessions, filter by user ID; the filter syncs to ?userId= in the URL (the user drawer View sessions button seeds this param). See Admin console.

Where do I see recent pairing codes (1.39.0)?
Open Admin console → Operations → Pairings (/pairings). The page loads GET /api/v1/admin/pairings (requires admin.read) and lists recent codes from PostgreSQL (default 100 rows; optional limit 1–500). Filter by device ID, owner user ID, or numeric code — filters sync to ?deviceId=, ?userId=, ?numericCode=. Row Device / User links open /devices?deviceId= and /users?userId= (device owner). Read-only — change length/TTL under System pairing policy; hosts generate codes on the Agent. See Admin console.

System pairing policy and Pairings row jumps (1.40.0)?
System → pairing-policy section Open pairings → /pairings; Pairings row Session → /sessions?sessionId=… when sessionId is present.

How do I filter consumed pairing codes or open Pairings from Overview/Devices (1.41.0)?
On Pairings, use the Consumed select (Consumed / Unused / All); it syncs to ?consumed=yes|no and GET /api/v1/admin/pairings (yes = consumedAt set). Also open from Overview → Pairings card, or Devices → Actions → Pairings (?deviceId= pre-filled). See Admin console.

How do I open Pairings from the user drawer or Orders from Membership (1.42.0)?
On Users, the detail drawer Open pairings → /pairings?userId=…; on Membership, Open orders in the header → /orders?userId=… (URL ?userId= or the commerce order userId on that page). See Admin console.

How do I open Membership from Orders or filter pairing audit (1.43.0)?
On Orders, row Membership in Actions → /membership?userId=… when the order has userId (pairs with Membership Open orders, 1.42.0). On Audit, action presets include pairing.create and pairing.join (server has logged these since 1.12.0). See Admin console.

Where is billing history on the Client membership page (1.43.0)?
The Web Client /membership page shows a muted footnote that past orders are for platform operators in Admin — no Admin link on that page. End users contact IT or sales; operators use Admin Orders / Membership. See Plans & billing.

What does the Admin 403 page offer (1.44.0)?
Forbidden shows Back to dashboard (→ /); signed-in users can Sign in with another account; otherwise Sign in. See Admin console.

How do Pairings header audit links work (1.44.0)?
On Pairings, Create audit / Join audit open /audit?action=pairing.create or pairing.join. See Admin console.

What does the monitor-wall info alert say (1.44.0)?
It explains that layout can be saved, plus tips for in-wall observe / enterprise multi-screen observe. Product capabilities and enablement: Device Fleet & Enterprise.

Already signed in on /login (1.45.0)?
You are redirected to the dashboard (/) with an “already signed in” link. See Admin console.

How do I quickly filter pairing audit actions (1.45.0)?
On Audit, under the action filter, click the pairing.create / pairing.join chips (same targets as the Pairings header audit links). See Admin console.

Why does System warn about webhook under enforce (1.47.0)?
When entitlementMode is enforce and the webhook secret is not configured, inbound POST /api/v1/commerce/webhooks/entitlement always returns 401 until the server has a non-empty ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The current viewer has no System warning UI; check webhookSecretConfigured via GET /api/v1/admin/system/entitlement. See Admin console; production checklist on Production payment readiness.

Do Orders and Users filters sync to the URL (1.47.0)?
Yes. Orders: id, userId, sku, provider, currency, status; Users: userId, email, status, plan, billingKind, orgId, planExpiry. Bookmark or share links; Membership / user drawer deep links still seed ?userId=. See Admin console.

Deploy & go-live

What to verify before production payments?
Walk Production payment readiness · Checklist (mock → sandbox → production). Merchant credentials and notify DNS are configured in your environment / Entitlement; follow the checklist for go-live.

Where is the 15-step remote control acceptance?
On a logged-in host Agent plus the Web controller, follow Remote control · Manual acceptance checklist. Sign out and sign in on the controller first so the ops JWT is fresh; use power/host dry-run env vars on dev machines.

What are the local Docker host ports?
See Docker deployment for the core + dev table (Postgres 5637, Redis 6380, Server 3000; optional turn / ai / recording / admin profiles on the same page). Production must not expose DB/Redis on the host.

What does pnpm assert:prod-env do?
Read-only check in deploy/ before production docker compose up: validates .env.prod.example required keys; when compose/.env.prod exists, rejects weak placeholders; with ENTITLEMENT_MODE=enforce, requires a non-empty ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Passing does not mean a production PSP is shipped. See Docker deployment · assert:prod-env and Production payment readiness.

Which MinIO endpoints for local recording?
Dev recording profile: server in compose → http://minio:9000; Desktop Agent on the host → http://127.0.0.1:19000; console 19001. The default production stack has no MinIO — use external S3. See Docker deployment · Recording (MinIO).

title: Device Fleet & Enterprise Capabilities
content:
Metadata	Value
Doc	User / customer-facing product capabilities
Version	1.1.0
Updated	2026-09-23
Plan	Primarily Enterprise (enabled after enterprise service is purchased)

1. What the product includes

VistaRemote is more than one-to-one remote desktop. For enterprises and edge sites, it includes a full Device Fleet capability set:

Capability	In one line	Typical use
1:1 remote desktop	High-quality view + keyboard/mouse + files / terminal	Support desks, break/fix
Group keyboard & mouse	One controller operates many authorized devices in sync	Lab tours, mass config, training
Batch commands	Notify, lock, reboot, open URL across devices	End-of-day lock, alerts, incident response
Multi-screen monitor wall	Low-cost thumbnail observe; click into HD control	NOC walls, edge-site patrol
Virtual display	Dedicated virtual screen for remote sessions	Helpdesk remote, unattended stations
Out-of-band (OOB)	Intel AMT power / BIOS / KVM (enterprise private deploy)	Machines that are powered off or pre-OS
Audit & RBAC	Traceable actions, org roles	Compliance, IT separation of duties

With VistaCast: Cast watches business video; Remote manages edge compute boxes — a natural B2B bundle (cameras + Edge AI Box + VistaRemote management).

2. Who gets it and how to enable

Capability family	Plan	How to enable
Core 1:1 remote	Free / Pro / Enterprise	Default product path
Fleet: group control, batch commands, wall, virtual display	Enterprise	Purchase enterprise service, then enable entitlements
OOB / AMT	Enterprise + private deployment	Defined in the contract and delivery scope
Larger wall slot counts	Enterprise contract add-on	Validate slots and SLA against purchase

Sales & delivery posture (product commitment)

The capabilities above are in product scope: you can present them in proposals and RFPs as “supported.”

After an enterprise purchase or signed contract, the team enables, tunes, or add-ons to the site’s needs. Some capabilities are delivered and accepted on the contract’s schedule.

Endpoint management can be priced on its own (per device / seat), not only as a remote-desktop checkbox.

Pricing and enablement: contact sales or your implementer. Overview: Plans & billing.

3. Monitor wall: observe cheaply, control when needed

Thumbnail wall (low-cost observe)
        ↓ anomaly
Click device (enterprise entitlement)
        ↓
High-quality Remote Session (control)

Mode	Purpose
Thumbnail observe	Low resolution / frame rate preview across many online devices
High-quality control	Click into a 720p / 1080p-class remote session

This separates “100 devices online” from “100 simultaneous HD streams.” The latter is a contract add-on, not a default catalog promise. Larger walls (market messaging often cites tens to ~100+ observe slots) can be enabled and validated under contract on the existing architecture.

Entry: Admin Monitor wall; click a live slot to open a control session. See Admin console.

4. Group control & batch commands

Batch commands

From My devices (Client) or Admin Devices, multi-select devices and send:

Desktop notification

Lock screen

Reboot / shutdown (typed confirm required)

Open an http(s) URL

Each device returns its own result; actions are audited.

Group keyboard & mouse

On My devices, select online computers and open multi-computer control (/control), then switch to Sync. Keyboard and mouse on the focused picture go to every device that has tapped Allow. Clipboard, files, and the terminal are not broadcast. Agents can disconnect at any time; unauthorized devices are never controlled implicitly. Without the group-control entitlement, only Focus mode is available.

5. Virtual display

The product supports a virtual display for remote sessions so work happens on a dedicated virtual screen and disturbs the physical desktop less. It works with privacy-screen and multi-display policies.

Enable after the enterprise virtual display entitlement is granted (Agent UI).

Windows is the priority delivery platform; other OSes follow the contract.

Driver / imaging integrations can be delivered after purchase against the site design.

6. Out-of-band (AMT and similar)

For powered-off or pre-OS machines, Enterprise private deployments can include out-of-band management (e.g. Intel AMT: power, BIOS, OOB KVM). The default cloud path focuses on online Agents; OOB is enabled under enterprise contract + private deployment.

title: Login and pairing
content:
Controller (Web / Android)

Open the Web Client (https://app.example.com or local http://localhost:5173) or the Android APK

Sign in on the VistaRemote branded login page (/login) — required before pairing or remote control
Preferred (unified identity): primary “Sign in / Register” → LuminaryWorks Logto (OIDC); this page is the product Headless entry (not Logto’s hosted UI as the main surface)

Local / private mode C / offline: expand “Local account” for email + password


Enter the Agent pairing code (6–8 digits). Codes are one-shot (PAIRING_CONSUMED); a class cannot share one code.

Wait for video, then control with mouse/keyboard

For multi-computer layout (Solo / Mosaic), Sync, and how to return after leaving the workspace, see Multi-computer workspace.

Production signaling requires a short-lived Signaling Ticket (issued on join; Agents get agentSignalingTicket when creating a pairing session).

Anonymous pairing join returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

Trial and plans

New users get a 7-day standard_7d trial (once per user per product)

After trial, free tier keeps 1:1 P2P; SFU needs upgrade

v1.0 billing is Admin plan grants (real payments in v1.1)

Developers / ops (local E2E)

End-user docs stop at pairing and control basics. For local 1:1 P2P acceptance — login, pairing, video, input, clipboard / files / terminal — use the Meta repo runbook:

plan/mvp-e2e-runbook.md (relative path in a Meta checkout: plan/mvp-e2e-runbook.md)

Production go-live: Meta plan/v1-golive-checklist.md. Ops-channel FRs: Meta spec/remote-session-ops-spec.md. SFU multi-viewer acceptance is not covered here.

Troubleshooting

Symptom	Hint
Cannot sign in	Check API URL; user may be disabled; IdP must be reachable for SSO
Pairing asks to log in	Session expired — sign in again
Pairing fails	Code expired or invalid
No video	TURN / UDP firewall; cellular needs TURN

title: Multi-computer workspace
content:
After pairing, you land in the multi-computer control workspace (/control). You can keep several computers connected at once (capped by your plan’s session allowance, maximum 8).

Viewer vs Web browser

Prefer the desktop Viewer for day-to-day remote control (LAN P2P, less background throttling, capture permissions). The Web Client at http://localhost:5173/control uses the same UI, but browser ICE / focus / permission limits often make input unreliable — use it for local UI checks, not as the primary control path.

Three concepts (do not mix them up)

Name	Layer	Meaning
Solo	View layout	One large stage; switch other connected PCs with tabs
Mosaic	View layout	All connected PCs previewed together; click a tile to send keyboard/mouse there
Sync	Input scope	Keyboard/mouse fan out to multiple PCs (needs Enterprise group-control entitlement). This is not the same as mosaic preview

Defaults: one computer → Solo; two or more → Mosaic. You can override in the toolbar; disconnecting all resets to the automatic default.

Leaving and returning

Session state lives outside the router. Visiting Home, Add-computer pairing, or Settings does not disconnect (unless you sign out, close the window, or disconnect explicitly).

Home shows Back to remote control

Other pages show a blue strip: remote control in progress → return

On the add-computer page, use Cancel — back to remote control

Use a Viewer / Web Client that loads the latest client build; restarting only the Server does not refresh the Viewer UI.

Shortcuts

Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+8 (or Cmd on macOS): focus the 1st–8th connected computer

Mosaic and bandwidth

With three or more full desktops open, non-focused tiles prefer the Fluent quality preset to save bandwidth; the focused tile keeps the quality you chose in the toolbar.

title: Production payment readiness (ops)
content:
Use this page to walk mock → sandbox → production. LuminaryWorks Entitlement already ships payment adapters; that is not live merchant enablement. Lite checkout (commerce complete / status, plus the Entitlement ingress webhook) can cache local User.plan. WeChat Pay / Alipay merchant onboarding, notify DNS, and production PSP secrets are owner-ops — configured in your environment / Entitlement. Product outbox delivery may still be in progress. Never commit merchant secrets.

Architecture: Commercial billing. Admin modules: Admin console. Spec: spec/billing-commerce-spec.md.

Membership vs wallet

VistaRemote has no prepaid wallet, balance, or top-up SKU. Buyers purchase Pro / Ultra subscription offerings (Client /membership → commerce BFF → Entitlement).

Sandbox path:

Sign in once with unified OIDC so users.logtoSub is set (commerce X-Act-As-Subject is the Logto sub, not the local User UUID)

Non-production Entitlement with PAYMENT_CONFIG_MASTER_KEY can auto-seed a mock payment config; or enable mock/alipay sandbox in Admin

Membership: pick SKU → payment method (mock preferred) → Complete payment; mock captures on complete and syncs local User.plan

Live WeChat/Alipay merchant onboarding remains Entitlement owner-ops; this product does not ship a cross-product wallet

Path: mock → sandbox → production

Stage	Typical config	Behavior
Mock (local)	ENTITLEMENT_MODE=off	Local orders and plans. The order owner may call POST /api/v1/billing/orders/:id/simulate-paid (Controller JWT). Admin Orders Simulate paid calls POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/simulate-paid and applies only to source=local_billing.
Sandbox	ENTITLEMENT_MODE=enforce, central Entitlement reachable	Web Client /membership: catalog providerHint wechat → wechat_pay_v3, alipay → alipay_f2f; may show QR / codeUrl / redirect. After pay the page polls GET .../orders/:id (~2s, ~2 min cap); return or Complete payment posts .../complete, then refreshes local entitlements. Sandbox secrets live on Entitlement, not this repo. Not production WeChat / Alipay merchant notify.
Production	Same mode + production Entitlement / PSP (owner-ops)	VistaRemote lite webhook POST /api/v1/commerce/webhooks/entitlement can sync User.plan. WeChat / Alipay platform notify lands on LuminaryWorks Entitlement, not VistaRemote. Real merchant onboarding, certificates, and platform callbacks are configured in your environment / Entitlement.

Lite ingress order.fulfilled (POST /api/v1/commerce/webhooks/entitlement) uses HMAC headers (FR-BILL-06) — not WeChat / Alipay platform notify verification:

Header	Requirement
content-type	application/json
x-lw-timestamp	Unix seconds (±300s window)
x-lw-nonce	≥8 chars; replay protection
x-lw-signature	v1=<base64url>
x-lw-event-id	Idempotent event id

Signature: HMAC-SHA256(ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET, timestamp.nonce.rawBody) → base64url; verify on the untouched raw body (never re-serialize JSON). ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET is this ingress HMAC secret and must equal Entitlement ENTITLEMENT_ORDER_FULFILLED_TARGETS.vistaremote.secret. Legacy X-Entitlement-Signature equality is a hard-cut 401 with no fallback. Missing secret → 401 (honest reject, not silent mock).

Fulfillment failures (local plan projection write) enter commerce_webhook_fulfillments retry; exhausted → dead letter. Admin: GET/POST /api/v1/admin/commerce-webhook/* (status / dead-letters / process-once / replay|ignore); audit commerce.webhook.* (FR-BILL-07).

Runbook: WeChat / Alipay merchant onboarding remains owner-ops and is not delivered with this repo.

Webhook user mapping (Logto sub)

After signature verification, order.fulfilled subjectId must be the Logto OIDC sub. The server resolves the local user via users.logtoSub (not the local User UUID; users are never auto-created).

User origin	logtoSub	Webhook can write User.plan
Web / OIDC login + POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/exchange	set	✓
Admin local register / Controller JWT only	often null	✗ → 400 WEBHOOK_USER_NOT_FOUND

For local-only users (no Logto binding), grant plans via:

Admin Users → change plan (Admin plan grant), or

Order owner commerce POST .../complete / GET .../orders/:id (CommercePlanSyncService.syncForAccessToken with the caller Bearer token)

Closed-trial paths: Meta-Repo plan/trial-ops-checklist.md.

VistaRemote server env names (names only)

Names below come from server source and server/.env.example. Do not invent values. Keep production secrets in a secret store / Entitlement host — not in git.

This repo has no COMMERCE_* environment variables. The commerce BFF forwards /v1/... using ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL.

Name	Role
ENTITLEMENT_MODE	off | shadow | enforce | offline_license
ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL	Central Entitlement base URL
ENTITLEMENT_SERVICE_API_KEY	M2M X-Service-Key
ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET	Lite ingress HMAC secret (= Entitlement TARGETS.vistaremote.secret); empty → webhook always 401
COMMERCE_WEBHOOK_POLL_MS	Fulfillment retry poll interval (default 15000; <=0 disables)
COMMERCE_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS	Fulfillment retry cap (default 5 → dead letter)
ENTITLEMENT_CACHE_TTL_MS	Entitlement cache TTL
ENTITLEMENT_OFFLINE_GRACE_MS	Offline grace
ENTITLEMENT_DEPLOYMENT_ID	Deployment id
ENTITLEMENT_LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEYS	Offline License public-key JSON (offline_license)
ENTITLEMENT_LICENSE_PAYLOAD	Offline License payload (offline_license)
ENTITLEMENT_LICENSE_ALLOW_GRACE	Offline License grace flag
PRODUCT_CODE	Product code (example: vistaremote)
BILLING_ALLOW_SIMULATE_PAID	Only when NODE_ENV=production: true re-enables simulate-paid. Production should omit it or leave it not true
NODE_ENV	production disables simulate-paid by default

WeChat / Alipay merchant ids, APIv3 keys, certificates, and Alipay app secrets belong on Entitlement / the PSP — not VistaRemote server env vars. ENTITLEMENT_TRIAL_PURGE_* is trial recording purge, not a payment callback.

Client Membership (sandbox, not PSP live)

Web Client /membership (the current viewer Admin has no /membership route):

Accept policies → pick a Pro/Ultra SKU → choose WeChat Pay or Alipay (catalog providerHint, not Entitlement adapter ids).

Checkout → POST /api/v1/commerce/orders then .../pay. A QR, payment link, or redirect may appear.

The page shows “Waiting for payment confirmation…” and polls order status; Complete payment also posts complete.

When status is paid / fulfilled / completed / success, entitlements refresh. The on-page sandbox note is not live merchant notify.

Closed trial can also grant via Admin Users → change plan, without checkout.

Checklist

System entitlement flags (FR-WAD-52): Admin System → entitlement/payment config. GET /api/v1/admin/system/entitlement returns only entitlementMode, entitlementBaseUrlConfigured, and webhookSecretConfigured. It must not include ENTITLEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET or a raw base URL. Use Copy entitlement status JSON to verify.

Reject a bad signature: POST /api/v1/commerce/webhooks/entitlement with a wrong or missing x-lw-signature (or legacy X-Entitlement-Signature only) → 401; local User.plan must not change. Unset secret → 401 as well.

Fulfillment dead letters (FR-BILL-07): Admin GET /api/v1/admin/commerce-webhook/dead-letters lists failures; process-once / replay / ignore available. WeChat / Alipay merchant onboarding remains owner-ops.

simulate-paid forbidden for commerce: Admin Simulate paid is shown only on local_billing pending rows. POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/simulate-paid on source=commerce returns 400 COMMERCE_SIMULATE_PAID_FORBIDDEN (UI: use Membership complete / webhook). Do not call POST /api/v1/billing/orders/:id/simulate-paid with an Admin JWT.

Disable simulate-paid in production: when NODE_ENV=production and BILLING_ALLOW_SIMULATE_PAID is not true, simulate-paid returns 400 SIMULATE_PAID_DISABLED (UI: simulate paid disabled in production).

Webhook user mapping: subjectId must be the Entitlement-side Logto sub with a matching local users.logtoSub; otherwise 400 WEBHOOK_USER_NOT_FOUND. Admin-created local users should use plan grant or Client Membership complete/status — not webhook auto-grant.

Grant path: after sandbox Client Membership pay + complete / status polling (or a signed lite webhook when the user is OIDC-bound), the Admin Users list shows the matching plan. That is a local cache, not proof that production PSP settlement is complete.

No secrets in git: .env, CI logs, and Admin JSON must not contain merchant secrets.

Not shipped (owner-ops)

Complete these on the LuminaryWorks Entitlement / PSP consoles. VistaRemote does not accept WeChat / Alipay platform notify; this repo only has lite POST /api/v1/commerce/webhooks/entitlement. No production merchant pack ships with VistaRemote:

WeChat merchant onboarding, APIv3 key and platform certs, payment notify URL on Entitlement

Alipay app and keys, face-to-face / sandbox → production cutover

Production credentials for PayPal / Wise and other channels

Store those secrets in the Entitlement environment (do not commit them in server/.env)

After onboarding, re-run this checklist: entitlement API flags, bad-signature 401, and commerce simulate-paid still forbidden.

title: Remote Control (User Guide)
content:
For operators using VistaRemote for remote assistance—not developers.

VistaRemote takes the logged-in desktop session tools operators use in MeshCentral / MeshAgent—screen, keyboard and mouse, clipboard, files, terminal, chat, processes, read-only services, power, host info, notify, lock, open URL, screenshot—and ships them here. Video uses WebRTC, not Mesh JPEG desktop or server byte relay.

VistaRemote is not full MeshCentral RMM. It does not include Intel AMT / IP-KVM, remote printing, registry, service start/stop, Wake-on-LAN magic packets, UAC/logon desktop, file clipboard, USB, audio mix, wallpaper toggle, remote script run, locking the host user’s input, or an Agent JS console.

AI assist (off by default)

Optional. See AI assist. When it is off, keyboard, mouse, chat, and the terminal behave as they do today. An alert does not start a remote session. The host must allow AI separately from remote control before any click or typing happens. Local Cursor or ChatGPT can use MCP on that already-allowed session only; it does not open a new one.

Roles

Role	Typical use
Host (agent)	Office PC runs Desktop Agent and shows a pairing code
Controller	Admin enters the code on phone/browser to view and control the desktop

How to connect (controller)

Method	Action
Numeric code	Enter 6–8 digits on /pairing
QR code	Scan code shown on host screen
Link	Open https://…/join/… or org short link

Web routes: /pairing, /join/{token}.

The Electron Viewer is the same Web controller in a desktop shell (same session ops sidebar). The mobile app can view the screen and send mouse/keyboard; this release has no files/terminal ops panel on mobile.

Controlling more than one computer

On My devices, select online computers and choose Control selected. That opens /control.

Mode	Who	Where keyboard and mouse go
Focus (default)	Accounts with a remote-session allowance	Only the computer you clicked
Sync	Enterprise group-control entitlement	From the focused picture to every computer that has tapped Allow

Clipboard, files, and the terminal stay on the focused computer. One window keeps at most 8 high-quality pictures, and never more than the plan's concurrent-session limit. Leaving the page to add another computer does not drop the ones already connected. Each host still has to tap Allow. This is not the thumbnail monitor wall.

Mapping from Mesh session tools

This is Mesh already-logged-in desktop (KVM session / toolbar / same-device terminal and files), not inventory RMM. These tools are available inside a VistaRemote session after the host clicks Allow and the account has the matching permission.

Typical Mesh capability	VistaRemote
Mouse / keyboard / wheel	Operate on the remote video
View only (no input)	Pairing page View only
Text clipboard	Clipboard side tab
Browse, upload/download, rename, copy	Files (user home jail)
Terminal / CMD / PowerShell	Terminal (Windows ConPTY / macOS·Linux PTY)
Session chat	Chat (the Agent window can reply)
Process list / end task	Processes
Service list	Services (read-only; no start/stop)
Reboot / shut down	Power (confirm; delayed a few seconds)
Host info, notify, lock, open http(s)	Host
Session screenshot	Toolbar Screenshot (PNG on the controller)
Consent / connection bar	Host Allow; always-on-top bar to disconnect
Multiple displays	Toolbar switch; multi-window up to 2 streams
Guest / share link	Pairing link / QR (one-shot, expires)

Intentionally not Mesh-parity (do not look for these in-session): Ctrl+Alt+Del / logon desktop, lock the remote user’s keyboard, wallpaper toggle, remote Run script, service start/stop, registry, remote print, Wake-on-LAN, AMT hardware KVM, USB, remote audio, JPEG quality presets, Agent console script push.

Quick steps

Host (Desktop)

Install VistaRemote Agent (Windows / macOS / Linux).

Sign in with your organization account (or register the device).

Note the pairing code on screen (often 6–8 digits, time-limited).

Share the code with the controller; approve when they connect before screen share starts.

Controller (Web or Mobile)

Open your organization’s VistaRemote URL (browser or app).

Enter the pairing code on the pairing page.

When status is connected, you can see and control the remote desktop.

Technical details: Pairing (developer-oriented).

Connection quality

Issue	Suggestion
Laggy video	Check network on both sides; IT may provide TURN
LAN only	Ask IT to allow UDP or deploy TURN
Multiple viewers	Requires Pro/Enterprise (SFU); may be limited after trial

Troubleshooting: stuck connecting and force-disconnect

Stuck on connecting: Check network, firewall UDP, and whether TURN is configured. Do not start by changing DNS. Admin System shows entitlement config flags (FR-WAD-52); ICE candidates still come from the Server. If it still fails, check UDP/firewall and TURN. See also FAQ.

Force-disconnect: Admins can force disconnect an active room from Sessions; the host can disconnect from the always-on-top connection bar.

Multiple displays (Web controller)

Single monitor: the host’s primary display is captured by default (no picker).

When the host has two or more monitors:

Action	Behavior
Picker / toolbar switch	Choose or switch the active remote display (single-stream On-Demand)
Multi-window	Up to 2 parallel streams (split pane or pop-out); each pane controls its own display
Exit multi-window	Back to one stream; toolbar switching still works
3+ monitors	P2P shows only 2 streams; use switch or later SFU for the rest

Host Agent

Closing the window keeps the Agent in the system tray; restore, disconnect, or quit from the tray.

Tray menu includes Open at login.

Linux: X11 / XWayland inject directly; pure Wayland needs Screen sharing + Remote Desktop portal consent. See Linux remote control.

Clipboard, files, terminal, chat, processes, services, power, and host (Web / Viewer)

After the session is connected and the host has armed control, the side panel can:

Sync plain-text clipboard both ways (host copies update the viewer)

List the host user home directory, upload/download, create folders, delete, rename, and copy (inside the jail; copy is files only)

Open an xterm user-session terminal (Windows ConPTY / POSIX PTY; for example echo / dir / tput cols)

Chat with the person at the host

List processes and end a task (not pid 1 or the Agent itself)

Read-only list of system services (no remote start/stop)

Reboot / shut down after a typed confirmation; the action is delayed several seconds

Read host info (name / OS / IP), send a desktop notification, and lock the screen (confirmation required)

Open an http/https URL in the host’s default browser (file: / javascript: are rejected)

Toolbar Screenshot: save the current frame as a PNG on the controller (not via the server)

Accounts without the matching permission do not see the terminal, services, power, or host tabs. Pairing with View only also hides those tabs and does not create a keyboard/mouse channel.

The host must Allow in the Agent window before keyboard, mouse, and ops channels work; View only keeps the video. The host desktop shows an always-on-top connection bar to disconnect. Inject and ops channels stop as soon as the session disconnects.

Manual acceptance checklist (one pass)

Run this on a logged-in Agent plus the Web controller. Sign out and sign in again first so the controller JWT includes ops permissions. For power and lock on a development machine, set VISTAREMOTE_POWER_DRY_RUN=1 and VISTAREMOTE_HOST_DRY_RUN=1 so the host is not actually rebooted or locked.

#	Step	Expected
1	Host shows a pairing code; controller joins via /pairing	Video appears; status connected
2	Host has not clicked Allow	Mouse/keyboard do nothing; ops ignored
3	Host clicks Allow	Input works; side tabs appear
4	Connection bar Disconnect	Inject stops immediately
5	Clipboard: send text / copy on host	Plain text both ways
6	Files: list, upload, download, mkdir, delete, rename, copy	All inside the home jail; .. cannot escape
7	Terminal: open xterm, run echo; enlarge the pane	Output; column count changes (tput cols)
8	Chat both ways	Visible on both; server audit has no body
9	Process list; end a test process you started	List refreshes; Agent cannot be killed
10	Services tab	Read-only list; no start/stop
11	Power (dry-run or real host)	Rejected without confirm; scheduled after confirm
12	Host: sysinfo, notify, lock (dry-run or real host)	Info visible; host shows a notification
13	Open https://example.com; try file://	First opens in the host browser; second errors
14	Toolbar Screenshot	PNG downloads locally
15	Pairing page: check View only, then join	No terminal / services / power / host tabs; no mouse/keyboard channel

Out of scope (do not test): Intel AMT / IP-KVM, Mesh JPEG KVM, remote printing, registry, service start/stop, Wake-on-LAN, UAC/logon desktop/Ctrl+Alt+Del, file clipboard, USB, audio mix, wallpaper toggle, remote scripts, locking the host keyboard.

Security

Do not share pairing codes with untrusted parties; codes expire and are one-shot (PAIRING_CONSUMED) — a class cannot reuse one code.

End the session and stop sharing when finished.

Enterprise editions may enable audit and behavior policies (admin-configured).
